jobs.title: Director, Product & Strategy
jobs.text:
Job Title: Director, Product & Strategy
Location: Hybrid (3 days per week) in Toronto / Greater Toronto Area (GTA), Ontario, Canada.
Candidates must reside in Toronto or the GTA and be legally authorized to work in Canada.
Travel: Approximately 10-20%
Employment Type: Permanent, Full-Time
Hiring Timeline: Immediate
Reporting Line: Head of Tech Delivery
Existing Vacancy: Yes. This posting is for an existing vacancy.
Application Deadline: Open until filled. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis.
Salary Range:
$140,000 - $160,000 CAD base per year, plus 15% bonus eligibility.
About Fulfillment IQ
Fulfillment IQ (FIQ) is a supply chain technology and consulting company helping retailers, brands, and 3PLs solve complex fulfillment and logistics challenges.
Our work spans three core practices: Supply Chain Consulting, Technology Delivery & Transformation, and Implementation. We help customers assess and design supply-chain strategies, select and implement technology, modernize fulfillment operations, and build technology solutions that solve complex operational challenges.
The Opportunity
We are looking for a Director, Product & Strategy to lead our Tech Delivery practice across both sides of the house: the internal teams that build, and the client relationships that fund and shape the work. This is a hands-on leadership role for someone who is equally comfortable in a client boardroom shaping strategy and in a delivery stand-up unblocking a team.
You will own the arc of a client engagement end to end: understanding the business problem, shaping the solution strategy, and directing the cross-functional team that delivers it, all while continuously deepening and expanding the client relationship. You will also help incubate Fulfillment IQ's own internal innovation products, applying the same product discipline to what we build for ourselves.
What You’ll Do
Client & Relationship Leadership
Own the client relationship as the senior point of contact for assigned clients, building trust with stakeholders from operators to executives.
Capture and translate client needs into clearly framed problems and solution strategies, translating business goals into delivery roadmaps.
Grow and expand accounts by identifying new opportunities, shaping proposals and statements of work, and converting successful delivery into expanded scope and long-term partnership.
Manage expectations, scope, risks, and escalations proactively, keeping engagements healthy commercially and operationally.
Delivery & Team Leadership
Lead and mentor cross-functional delivery teams, product managers, business analysts, UX designers, DevOps engineers, developers (front-end, back-end, full-stack), and tech leads.
Direct delivery across engagements, planning, resourcing, quality, timelines, and budgets, and holding teams accountable to outcomes.
Establish delivery standards, ways of working, and reusable practices that raise quality and predictability across the practice.
Attract and develop talent, coaching leads, growing capability, and building a team people want to be part of.
Product & Solution Strategy
Shape solution architectures and product strategies that fit each client's operations, budget, and roadmap.
Incubate Fulfillment IQ's internal innovation products, owning discovery, prioritization, and delivery of what we build for our own IP and platforms.
Translate supply chain and fulfillment technology trends into practical recommendations and differentiated offerings.
Partner closely with sales, partnerships, and leadership to align solutions with market opportunity.
What You'll Bring
8+ years of relevant experience, including leadership of technology delivery, product, or professional-services teams (services, consulting, systems-integration, or product backgrounds all welcome).
Proven ability to manage senior client relationships and grow accounts, turning delivery success into expanded scope and revenue.
Strong command of software delivery: product management, requirements, UX, and engineering across the full stack, plus modern DevOps and agile practices.
Experience shaping solution strategy and translating ambiguous business problems into clear, deliverable roadmaps.
A track record of leading and developing cross-functional teams and setting delivery standards.
Supply chain, fulfillment, logistics, WMS/OMS/TMS, or e-commerce technology experience strongly preferred.
Product ownership instincts: comfortable driving internal innovation products from idea to launch.
Excellent communication and executive presence; able to move fluidly between strategy conversations and hands-on delivery.
Bachelor's degree in a related field, or equivalent experience; based in the US or Canada and able to work on a hybrid schedule.
Skills and Competencies
Required Skills
Client & stakeholder management: building and expanding senior relationships and negotiating scope.
Delivery & program management: planning, resourcing, budgeting, risk management, and on-time execution across concurrent engagements.
Solution & product strategy: framing ambiguous business problems and translating them into architectures and roadmaps.
Cross-functional team leadership: directing product, BA, UX, engineering, and DevOps talent.
Software delivery lifecycle fluency: agile/scrum, requirements, UX, and full-stack engineering across front-end, backend, and DevOps.
Commercial acumen: proposals, statements of work, estimation, and account growth.
Executive communication & presentation: clear, credible, and persuasive with technical and business audiences.
Product ownership: prioritization, discovery, and driving products from concept to launch.
Good-to-Have Skills
Supply chain / fulfillment domain: WMS, OMS, TMS, order management, or e-commerce logistics platforms.
Pre-sales & solutioning: shaping deals and demonstrating solutions to prospective clients.
Modern cloud & DevOps tooling: CI/CD, containers, and cloud platforms (AWS, Azure, or GCP).
Product & delivery tooling: Jira, roadmapping, and agile management platforms.
Data & analytics literacy: using metrics to steer delivery and inform product decisions.
Relevant certifications: PMP, SAFe, CSM/CSPO, or equivalent.
Nice-to-Have Skills
Experience at a technology consultancy, systems integrator, or 3PL/retail technology organization.
Pre-sales / solutioning experience and familiarity with SOW and commercial models.
Hands-on background in one or more delivery disciplines (product, engineering, UX, or DevOps).
Why Fulfillment IQ
You will have the opportunity to help grow our implementation business, develop important client relationships, and contribute to how we approach the market.
Work with experienced implementation leaders who understand the platforms and the operations they support.
Sell services that address practical warehouse challenges and make a visible difference to clients.
Have a voice in account priorities, partner relationships, and the development of the practice.
Work with colleagues who value direct communication, sound judgment, and accountability.
Health and Wellness
Comprehensive extended health and dental coverage for you and your family
Employee wellness programs where applicable
Time Off
Competitive paid time off, sick leave, and public holidays
Flexible leave policies that respect local labour standards
Retirement and Financial Security
CPP contributions and a group retirement savings plan with employer contributions
Employee stock options (ESOP), where applicable
Professional Growth
Dedicated learning and development budget, with support for skills, leadership, and career progression
Flexible Work
Remote and hybrid work options, flexible hours aligned to role and client needs
Additional Perks
Equipment and workstation allowances, internet and business travel reimbursements, team events and offsites
Work Authorization
Applicants must be legally authorized to work in Canada.
Use of Artificial Intelligence in Hiring:
FIQ uses artificial intelligence to assist in the screening, assessment, and shortlisting of applications for this position, including features within our applicant tracking system. AI supports human reviewers and does not make hiring decisions on its own. Final hiring decisions are made by FIQ personnel. If you have questions about how AI is used in this process, contact hr@fulfillmentiq.com.
Accommodations:
FIQ is committed to an inclusive and accessible recruitment process. Consistent with the Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act (AODA) and the Ontario Human Rights Code, accommodations are available on request at any stage of recruitment and assessment. Contact hr@fulfillmentiq.com and we will work with you to meet your needs.
Candidate Privacy:
Your personal information is collected and used for recruitment purposes in accordance with FIQ's Candidate Privacy Notice, available here, and in accordance with applicable Canadian privacy law (PIPEDA). This includes the use of AI-assisted screening described above and cross-border storage or processing that may occur in the United States. By applying, you acknowledge this notice. Questions: hr@fulfillmentiq.com.
Equal Opportunity:
Fulfillment IQ is a people-first company built on trust, collaboration, and ownership. We are proud to be an equal opportunity employer and are committed to building a diverse, inclusive, and high-performing workplace. We consider all qualified applicants without regard to any ground protected under the Ontario Human Rights Code, including race, ancestry, place of origin, colour, ethnic origin, citizenship, creed, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, marital status, family status, or disability.
Learn More About Us:
Website: fulfillmentiq.com
LinkedIn: Fulfillment IQ
Spotify: eCom Logistics Podcast Spotify
YouTube: eCom Logistics Podcast YouTube

jobs.title: Director, Services Technology Risk
jobs.text:
Our Purpose
Mastercard powers economies and empowers people in 200+ countries and territories worldwide. Together with our customers, we’re helping build a sustainable economy where everyone can prosper. We support a wide range of digital payments choices, making transactions secure, simple, smart and accessible. Our technology and innovation, partnerships and networks combine to deliver a unique set of products and services that help people, businesses and governments realize their greatest potential.
Title and Summary
Director, Services Technology RiskWho is Mastercard?
Mastercard is a global technology company in the payments industry. Our mission is to connect and power an inclusive, digital economy that benefits everyone, everywhere by making transactions safe, simple, smart, and accessible. Using secure data and networks, partnerships and passion, our innovations and solutions help individuals, financial institutions, governments, and businesses realize their greatest potential.
Our decency quotient, or DQ, drives our culture and everything we do inside and outside of our company. With connections across more than 210 countries and territories, we are building a sustainable world that unlocks priceless possibilities for all.
Overview:
The Services Technology Risk team is looking for a Director, Service Technology Risk professional to help maintain secure, resilient, and trusted technology environments while enabling innovation and growth.
The ideal candidate is analytical, collaborative, and proactive, with a passion for identifying and managing risks, strengthening controls, and partnering with Engineering, Product, Security, and Business teams. This role will focus on improving risk management and assurance practices through automation, analytics, and scalable solutions while supporting regulatory, audit, and customer expectations.
Role:
The Director, Services Technology Risk will lead the identification, assessment, prioritization, monitoring, and escalation of technology and operational risks across Services. This role will develop risk management strategies and frameworks, including risk registers, product risk assessments, and risk and control self-assessments, providing leadership with clear insights to support informed decisions.
The role will partner with Product, Engineering, and Security teams to embed risk management into business and technology processes, strengthen accountability, and ensure risks are effectively managed. The ideal candidate brings deep technology risk expertise, strong business judgment, and the ability to influence senior stakeholders, translate complex risks into business impact, and build scalable capabilities that support secure innovation and growth.
The Director, Technology Risk Identification & Assessment will:
• Lead the Risk Identification and Assessment for Services, establishing the strategy, operating model, governance, and capabilities required to consistently identify, assess, prioritize, monitor, and manage technology and operational risk.
• Establish and mature standardized risk management practices across Services, including risk registers, product risk assessments, Risk and Control Self-Assessments (RCSAs), and risk acceptance and escalation.
• Modernize and scale risk identification and assessment through automation, analytics, and AI-enabled capabilities that improve the quality, timeliness, and efficiency of risk management.
• Maintain a consolidated view of material risks across Services products, platforms, and programs, ensuring clear ownership, accountability, and visibility into risk exposure, treatment, and status.
• Partner with Product and Engineering leaders to embed risk identification and assessment into business and technology processes, reinforcing their accountability for managing risks throughout the risk lifecycle.
• Provide effective risk challenge and judgment on material and emerging risks, including cybersecurity, resilience, regulatory, operational, and risks introduced by emerging technologies such as AI/ML and generative AI.
• Establish governance for residual risk acceptance and escalation, ensuring decisions are transparent, appropriately approved, aligned with established risk appetite and tolerance, and supported by clear ownership and rationale.
• Translate complex technology risks into clear business impact, tradeoffs, and actionable insights to support leadership decision-making, prioritization, investment, and remediation.
• Provide Services leadership with an integrated view of the risk profile, including material exposures, emerging risks, accepted risks, trends, and areas requiring management attention.
• Partner across Engineering, Product, Security, Business, and enterprise risk functions to drive consistent risk practices, reduce fragmentation and duplication, and strengthen overall risk management across Services.
• Lead and develop a team of technology risk professionals, fostering strong risk judgment, constructive challenge, accountability, and trusted partnerships across the organization.
All About You:
• Significant experience in technology risk management, operational risk, information security risk, technology audit, technology controls, or a related discipline.
• Strong experience leading and maturing technology risk management practices across complex products, platforms, and business environments, such as risk register management, product risk Assessments, RCSAs, and other risk identification and assessment activities.
• Comfortable navigating ambiguity, resolving competing priorities, and establishing structure where processes are not yet mature.
• Strong interest in automation, analytics, and AI-enabled approaches to modernizing risk management.
• Strong understanding of technology risks across areas such as cybersecurity, data protection, software development, cloud services, identity and access management, vulnerability management, change management, third-party risk, and operational resilience.
• Ability to understand complex technology architectures and translate technical risks into clear business impact and decision points.
• Familiarity with regulatory expectations and data-residency requirements as they apply to technology controls, and with frameworks such as NIST, ISO 27001, and COBIT.
• Strong business judgment, with the ability to assess risk, challenge assumptions, evaluate tradeoffs, and provide practical recommendations.
• Demonstrated ability to influence senior Product, Engineering, Business, Security, and risk stakeholders.
• Ability to build practical and scalable operating models in complex or evolving environments.
• Proven experience leading, coaching, and developing high-performing teams.
• Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to communicate complex risk matters clearly to technical and non-technical audiences.
• Bachelor’s degree required.
• Professional certifications such as CISA, CISSP, CRISC, CISM, or equivalent are preferred but not required.Mastercard is a merit-based, inclusive, equal opportunity employer that considers applicants without regard to gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, race, ethnicity, disabled or veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law. We hire the most qualified candidate for the role. In the US or Canada, if you require accommodations or assistance to complete the online application process or during the recruitment process, please contact and identify the type of accommodation or assistance you are requesting. Do not include any medical or health information in this email. The Reasonable Accommodations team will respond to your email promptly.
Corporate Security Responsibility
All activities involving access to Mastercard assets, information, and networks comes with an inherent risk to the organization and, therefore, it is expected that every person working for, or on behalf of, Mastercard is responsible for information security and must:
Abide by Mastercard’s security policies and practices;
Ensure the confidentiality and integrity of the information being accessed;
Report any suspected information security violation or breach, and
Complete all periodic mandatory security trainings in accordance with Mastercard’s guidelines.
In line with Mastercard’s total compensation philosophy and assuming that the job will be performed in the US, the successful candidate will be offered a competitive base salary and may be eligible for an annual bonus or commissions depending on the role. The base salary offered may vary depending on multiple factors, including but not limited to location, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. Mastercard benefits for full time (and certain part time) employees generally include: insurance (including medical, prescription drug, dental, vision, disability, life insurance); flexible spending account and health savings account; paid leaves (including 16 weeks of new parent leave and up to 20 days of bereavement leave); 80 hours of Paid Sick and Safe Time, 25 days of vacation time and 5 personal days, pro-rated based on date of hire; 10 annual paid U.S. observed holidays; 401k with a best-in-class company match; deferred compensation for eligible roles; fitness reimbursement or on-site fitness facilities; eligibility for tuition reimbursement; and many more. Mastercard benefits for interns generally include: 56 hours of Paid Sick and Safe Time; jury duty leave; and on-site fitness facilities in some locations.THIS POSTING RELECTS ONE OR MORE CURRENT VACANCIES ON OUR TEAM, AND MASTERCARD INTENDS TO FILL THIS POSITION BY 01/18/2027. If the fill date has passed, Mastercard intends to fill this position as soon as possible.
Pay Ranges
Remote - California: $142,000 - $234,000 USD
Job Posting Window
Posting windows may change based on the volume of applications received and business necessity. Candidates are encouraged to apply expeditiously.

jobs.title: VP Senior Software Developer Analytics, Platforms, Applications
jobs.text:
We are a leading global asset management firm with over 3,000 employees across 20 offices in 15 countries; we help millions of investors around the world pursue their financial goals.
We hire critical thinkers. People who thrive in a collaborative culture like ours where we solve real problems while building the future of finance.
You
Are excited to be part of a vibrant engineering community that values diversity, hard work, and continuous learning.
Love solving complex real-world business problems.
Recognize that cross-functional collaboration is a core component of success for the team.
Believe there are multiple ways to solve most technical problems and are willing to debate the trade-offs.
Have become a stronger engineer by making mistakes and learning from them.
Are a doer, someone who wants to grow their career and gain experience across technologies and business functions.
We
Continuously invest in a high-performance and inclusive culture, in which a diversity of backgrounds, experiences and viewpoints are celebrated and valued.
Encourage career mobility, so you can benefit from learning different functions and technologies, and we gain the benefits of your experience across teams.
Run technology pro bono programs that help the non-profit community and give our engineering community opportunities to volunteer and participate.
Offer education reimbursements and ongoing training in technology, communication, and diversity & inclusion.
Embrace knowledge sharing through lunch-and-learns, demos, and technical forums.
Consider our people to be our greatest asset—we will help you learn what PIMCO Technology has to offer so you can participate in activities that benefit your career while delivering impactful technology solutions.
We are seeking a VPlevel Senior Software Developer to lead development and implementation of analytics tools and APIs for quants and portfolio managers.
You will provide technical leadership while remaining handson: design, build, test, and deploy scalable frontend UIs, highperformance backend services, and APIs; translate quant and portfoliomanager requirements into technical designs; collaborate with engineering, quant teams, and portfolio managers to define scope and priorities; own delivery, production reliability, and incident response; and mentor peers.
Required Experience
Strong Python proficiency, advanced SQL for complex data analysis, 10+ years of software engineering experience delivering production systems, and experience with cloud platforms (AWS preferred).
Familiarity with quantitative workflows or direct experience working with quant teams is required.
Preferred: distributed systems or largescale data processing, containerization (Docker/Kubernetes), and CI/CD. Frontend JavaScript experience is a plus.
The role requires clear communication, results orientation, and willingness to take on multiple roles to deliver solutions under time pressure.
Technical Skills/Qualifications
BS/MS degree in Computer Science, Mathematics or related technical field.
10+ years of hands-on software development experience.
Strong Python Proficiency is essential.
Strong Pandas and SQL proficiency is essential.
Familiarity with distributed systems, large scale data processing, and containerization (Docker/Kubernetes) a plus.
Front end development experience a plus.
Familiarity with cloud platforms (AWS) is a plus.
PIMCO follows a total compensation approach when rewarding employees which includes a base salary and a discretionary bonus. Base salary is the fixed component of compensation that is determined by core job responsibilities, relevant experience, internal level, and market factors. The discretionary bonus is used to award performance and therefore is determined by company, business, team, and individual performance.
Salary Range: $ 175,000.00 - $ 240,000.00

PIMCO recruits and hires qualified candidates without regard to race, national origin, ancestry, religion (including religious dress and grooming practices), sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, breastfeeding, or related medical conditions), sexual orientation, gender (including gender identity and expression), age, military or veteran status, disability (physical or mental), any factor prohibited by law, and as such affirms in policy and practice to support and promote the concept of equal employment opportunity and affirmative action, in accordance with all applicable federal, state, provincial and municipal laws. The company also prohibits discrimination on other basis such as medical condition, or marital status under applicable laws.
Applicants with Disabilities
PIMCO is an Equal Employment Opportunity/Affirmative Action employer. We provide reasonable accommodation for qualified individuals with disabilities, including veterans, in job application procedures. If you have any difficulty using our online system due to a disability and you would like to request an accommodation, you may contact us at 949-720-7744 and leave a message. jobs.title: Director of Product
jobs.text:
Orcrist is building a next generation data intelligence platform using cutting-edge technologies. We're handling petabyte-scale data with sub-second queries. Our product is a Kubernetes‑based platform delivered as B2B SaaS or as a self‑hosted on‑prem solution, including air‑gapped deployments. We enable customers across defense, law enforcement, and enterprise to turn mission-critical data into actionable intelligence.
Role
As Director of Product you own Orcrist’s entire product portfolio - Orcrist’s OIP and Civitas’ Sentinel, and lead the product organisation. You decide what Orcrist builds and in which order: what becomes platform and what stays customer-specific, which customer problem is solved next, and how we measure that it has been solved. Our promise is demonstrable the effectiveness of our software, and making that promise deliverable is the core of this role. You work directly with Engineers, our Government Development-Team and our customers and report to the COO of Orcrist.
What you’ll do
Own product strategy and the portfolio roadmap across all product lines – including the decision about what becomes shared platform and what remains customer-specific engineering.
Build and lead the product organisation: hire and develop Product Managers for the product lines and align them on common standards for discovery, prioritisation and delivery.
Make product effectiveness and customer activity & usage a measurable product goal: define metrics, measurement logic and the subsequent tasks that are triggered by that.
Own discovery with our Government Development team and our customers, and translate their requirements into product decisions rather than collecting feature requests.
Decide prioritisation across competing customer, tender and platform demands, and defend those decisions to customers, the team and the management.
Plan deliverable releases together with Engineering and QA, holding the balance between speed, quality and platform capability.
Assess market, competitive and technology developments in the defence and simulation space and feed them into product strategy.
About you
8+ years of product management experience with complex technical products, preferably in the Analytics or SAAS-space, including several years leading Product Managers or a product organisation.
Proven track record of delivering products from discovery through to customer rollout – with nameable outcomes, not just roadmaps.

jobs.title: Chief Technology Officer
jobs.text:
Purpose
The Chief Technology Officer (CTO) will lead the institutions digital transformation and technology strategy, ensuring robust, secure, and scalable technology infrastructure that supports business objectives, regulatory compliance, and customer satisfaction. The CTO will also assume executive responsibility for Information Security, overseeing the protection of digital assets, data, and systems against cyber threats in alignment with regulatory standards and industry best practices. The CTO will lead the Information Technology Department, which comprises specialized teamsresponsible for the following functional areas:
1. IT Governance, Policy Development, and Project Management
2. Core Business Systems and Application Development
3. IT Operations and Service Delivery Management
4. Infrastructure, Network Administration, and Information Security
Key Outputs
A future-proof, secure IT environment supporting financial operations and customer interactions
Digitally enhanced customer, partner, and employee experiences
Regulatory compliance in all IT and cybersecurity operations (e.g., QCB, AML/CFT, data privacy)
Strategic oversight of the institutions Information Security framework and risk posture
Efficient execution of IT plans, budgets, reports, and resource allocation
Key Accountabilities and Responsibilities
1-Technology Strategy & Planning
Define and execute the Companys technology and digital transformation roadmap
Ensure alignment of IT initiatives with strategic business goals and compliance requirements
Lead enterprise-wide IT budgeting, planning, and performance tracking
Introduce emerging technologies that improve operational efficiency and customer engagement
2. Information Security Leadership
Serve as the executive responsible for developing and overseeing the Companys Information Security strategy
Ensure the implementation and continuous improvement of information security policies, controls, and incident response plans
Oversee regulatory compliance with cybersecurity frameworks (e.g., ISO 27001, QCB ICT & Cybersecurity Circulars, NIST)
Direct periodic security assessments, penetration tests, and IT risk audits
Establish a security-conscious culture and ensure all staff are trained in information security responsibilities
3. Core Systems & Applications Oversight
Oversee development, customization, and support of core business applications including remittance, forex, and compliance systems
Ensure business continuity, high system availability, and secure integrations with thirdparty platforms
Drive cloud adoption, system automation, and customer-facing technology enhancements
4. IT Operations, Governance & Compliance
Ensure effective and secure operation of IT infrastructure including servers, networks,databases, and cloud environments
Maintain governance over IT service delivery, change management, and regulatory reporting
Ensure audit readiness and oversee compliance with QCB guidelines and data protection laws
5. Vendor & External Partner Management
Lead evaluation, selection, and performance monitoring of IT vendors and service providers
Negotiate service level agreements (SLAs) and ensure contract compliance
Manage outsourced services and third-party risks related to IT and cybersecurity
6. Stakeholder Engagement
Collaborate with top management, compliance, AML, risk, finance, and operations departments
Provide periodic updates to the Board or Executive Committee on IT and information security posture
Liaise with regulators and auditors on matters related to technology and security
7. Leadership and Talent Development
Lead and develop a high-performing IT and cybersecurity team
Promote continuous learning, technical excellence, and innovation
Establish a performance-driven culture that encourages accountability, agility, and secure practices
Performance Standards:
Successful implementation of IT and digital transformation strategies
Demonstrated compliance with cybersecurity and regulatory requirements
High system availability, service reliability, and data integrity
Zero tolerance for major security breaches or audit non-compliance
Achievement of digital service KPIs for both internal users and customers
Key Competencies
Advanced understanding of IT infrastructure, cloud platforms, and system architecture
Deep knowledge of cybersecurity principles, tools, and frameworks (ISO, NIST, CIS controls)
Strong business acumen with the ability to build internal and external partnerships and lead technology-driven changes in a multicultural environment.
In-depth understanding of emerging technologies and trends, including Artificial Intelligence (AI), Machine Learning (ML), Internet of Things (IoT), and Business Intelligence(BI) tools, along with their potential applications.
Familiarity with financial technologies including AML systems, transaction monitoring, and API-based integrations
Strong command of IT risk management, disaster recovery, and data privacy standards
Proven strategic thinking, decision-making, and stakeholder management capabilities
Excellent communication skills with the ability to translate technical risk into business
language
Skilled in cross-functional leadership and building collaborative partnerships
Qualifications & Experience
Masters degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, or a related discipline
Minimum of 10 years of progressive IT experience, including at least 5 years in senior leadership within a financial institution
Substantial experience in enterprise IT security, digital transformation, and infrastructure management
Certifications such as CISM, CISSP, PMP, ITIL, ISO 27001, AWS/Azure Architect are strongly preferred
Demonstrated ability to manage technology governance, audit compliance, and vendor ecosystems.
Originally posted on Himalayas

jobs.title: SVP, Engineering
jobs.text:
About the company
At Covera Health, we're on a mission to improve healthcare by making every diagnosis more accurate.
Every year, millions of patients receive imaging that shapes life changing medical decisions. Yet too often, important findings are missed, patients struggle to access high quality imaging, and the healthcare system treats radiology like a commodity instead of one of the most critical moments in a patient's care journey.
We're changing that.
Covera combines clinical expertise, advanced AI, and one of the industry's largest radiology quality datasets to help detect disease earlier, improve diagnostic accuracy, and give clinicians greater confidence in every decision they make. Better diagnoses lead to better treatment, fewer unnecessary procedures, lower healthcare costs, and, most importantly, better outcomes for patients.
In 2026, Covera and Medmo came together to create the first platform designed to support the entire radiology journey. From helping patients find and schedule high quality imaging, to coordinating care, to ensuring the accuracy of every diagnosis, we're building a connected experience that simply hasn't existed before.
Backed by Insight Partners, our platform supports nearly 6 million people across Fortune 10 and Fortune 100 employers, three of the five largest national health plans, and thousands of value based primary care physicians.
This is an exciting moment to join Covera. We're building technology that is helping detect serious conditions earlier, improving the quality of care for millions of patients, and redefining what healthcare can be. If you're excited by meaningful work, ambitious teammates, and the opportunity to help save lives through better healthcare, we'd love to meet you.
About the role
As Senior Vice President of Engineering, you will lead Covera Health's Engineering and Platform/IT organizations, with direct ownership of our technology architecture, engineering standards, and technical execution. You will lead a technology organization of approximately 30 people, including Engineering and AI, and play an active role in the technical decisions that shape our products and platforms.
Reporting to the Chief Product & Technology Officer, you will serve as a deeply technical and operational partner to a strategically focused technology executive. You will own day-to-day engineering execution, architecture, technical quality, and reliability, making decisions independently while working closely with the CPTO on broader product and technology strategy.
You will lead a small but mighty team, leveraging modern AI-powered development practices and state-of-the-art tools to accelerate development, improve efficiency, and deliver high-quality solutions. This is a hands-on technical leadership role. You will stay close to the work, participating in architecture and design reviews, working through complex data platform challenges, and helping teams resolve critical production issues.
As a senior technology leader with strong product instincts, you will connect technology decisions to customer and business needs. You will serve as a critical bridge between Engineering and teams across the company, ensuring technical decisions support the products we're building and the problems we're solving for customers and patients.
In this role, you will be expected to:
Lead a technology organization of approximately 30 people across Engineering, AI, and Platform/IT, remaining closely involved in architecture, technical decisions, and engineering execution.
Partner with the CPTO to turn product and company strategy into technical execution, independently owning engineering decisions, architecture, technical quality, and day-to-day delivery.
Lead and develop a small group of engineering leaders while staying directly connected to the teams and the technical challenges they are solving.
Improve engineering effectiveness through strong technical practices, clear priorities, practical processes, and a focus on delivering reliable, high-quality software.
Bring strong product judgment to technology decisions, ensuring Engineering understands the customer, product, and business context behind what we build and how we prioritize.
Serve as a key bridge between Engineering and Product, Data, AI, Clinical, Operations, Security, and other teams, working directly with stakeholders to solve problems, prioritize technical investments, and move work forward.
Own technical architecture and engineering standards across application development, cloud infrastructure, data platforms and pipelines, integrations, and enterprise technology. Stay actively involved in design reviews and complex technical decisions.
Ensure Covera's platforms and systems can scale reliably and securely as our products, customers, data sources, and partnerships grow.
Set and maintain a high engineering bar, actively reviewing architecture and technical approaches to ensure solutions balance performance, scalability, reliability, security, cost, and speed.Recruit, develop, and retain exceptional technology talent while building a technically strong team that values ownership, collaboration, and engineering excellence.
Build a culture where engineers take ownership, make sound technical decisions, and remain focused on delivering meaningful product and business outcomes.Ensure Covera's technology organization can support increasingly complex data and AI-driven products while meeting the privacy, security, reliability, and quality requirements of healthcare.
Communicate technical decisions, priorities, risks, and tradeoffs clearly to both engineering teams and executive stakeholders.
Remain actively involved in diagnosing and resolving complex technical challenges, including data pipeline issues, architectural decisions, system performance, and critical production incidents.
Requirements:
15+ years of progressive software engineering and technology experience, including deep technical experience building and operating complex software systems and leading engineering teams.
Experience leading engineering teams and engineering managers while remaining actively involved in technical architecture, design, and execution.
Demonstrated success building technically strong, high-performing engineering teams with a culture of ownership, accountability, and high engineering standards..
Strong product instincts and demonstrated ability to connect technology strategy and execution to product, customer, and business needs.
Demonstrated ability to partner closely with Product leadership and operate effectively at the intersection of product and engineering.
Deep technical expertise and strong architectural judgment, with the ability and desire to remain actively involved in design reviews, technical problem-solving, and critical engineering decisions.
Experience building, scaling, and operating large-scale, data-intensive production systems and platforms.
Deep technical knowledge of modern software engineering, cloud infrastructure, data platforms and pipelines, integrations, security, reliability, and data architecture.
Experience improving engineering quality, reliability, and delivery through strong technical practices, effective tooling, and practical team leadership.
Demonstrated ability to make complex cross-functional decisions, resolve competing priorities, and create alignment across multiple teams and functions.
Experience working with ML/AI engineering teams or overseeing products and platforms incorporating AI/ML capabilities.
Strong track record of recruiting, developing, and retaining exceptional engineering leaders and talent.
Experience operating in fast-paced startup or growth-stage environments.
Excellent executive communication and cross-functional leadership skills.
Experience building or leading modern, data-intensive technology platforms, with a strong understanding of complex data pipelines, distributed systems, and production reliability.
Demonstrated ability to balance technical depth with leadership responsibilities, remaining close to engineering work while guiding teams and making broader technology decisions.
Preferred Qualifications:
Experience at a healthcare technology or data company building modern software platforms or technically complex products using clinical, imaging, or claims data.
Experience with healthcare or clinical data environments, including familiarity with HL7 and/or DICOM.
Experience with modern data and analytics platforms such as Databricks, Spark, or similar technologies.
Experience with AWS or equivalent cloud infrastructure.
Experience transitioning from a highly technical engineering environment into a leadership role at a startup or growth-stage company.
Experience developing engineering depth and technical leadership at a large-scale technology company, followed by engineering leadership experience in a smaller, product-focused organization.
AI at Covera
At Covera Health, AI is not a novelty. It's a core part of how we work. Every team member is expected to actively use AI in their day-to-day role, and we invest in building that fluency across the organization. If you lean into new tools and are energized by what's still possible, you'll fit in.
Benefits
Comprehensive medical plans - choose from three plans, including one with 100% of premiums covered for you and your dependents
Vision & Dental
Flexible Time Off - take the time you need, when you need it
Generous company wide holidays - 16 in total
401(k) Retirement Plan
Annual Professional Development Stipend to invest in courses, books, or any other professional development related activity
Annual Wellness stipend for fitness, mental health or other wellness expenses
We may use automated tools or AI to assist in reviewing applications.
At Covera Health, we strive to build diverse teams that reflect the people we want to empower through our technology. We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, disability, gender identity, or Veteran status. Equal Opportunity is the Law, and Covera Health is proud to be an equal-opportunity workplace and affirmative action employer. If you have a specific need that requires accommodation, please let a member of the People Team know.

Excellent executive communication and cross-functional leadership skills.

jobs.title: Senior Director, Finance - Product & Technology - Digital Business (Remote, US)
jobs.text:
Lumen is the trusted network for the AI‑powered world, connecting people, data, and applications through our expansive fiber network and connected ecosystem. We enable secure, high‑performance connectivity across cloud, edge, and AI workloads for enterprises, governments, and communities.
At Lumen, you’ll work on infrastructure customers rely on today and build for what’s next, where performance, security, and resilience matter.
This is a high accountability environment where bold ideas drive real innovation for our customers, partners, and industry. The work is challenging, expectations are clear, and trust is built into how we operate. If you’re ready to take ownership, deliver meaningful impact, and help shape the future of AI‑ready connectivity, join us today.
The Role
Lumen is seeking a strategic, forward-thinking Senior Director of Finance to serve as the CFO and trusted business partner for our Product & Technology organization. This executive-level leader will provide financial leadership across a dynamic portfolio of digital, software, platform, cloud, and technology investments, helping shape decisions that accelerate growth, enhance profitability, and maximize shareholder value.
In this highly visible role, you will partner directly with executive leadership to drive financial strategy, long-range planning, investment prioritization, and business performance. You will lead a high-performing finance organization while influencing critical decisions related to product innovation, technology investments, resource allocation, and long-term growth.
Responsibilities
Serve as the strategic finance leader and key business partner to Product & Technology leadership, translating business priorities into actionable financial strategies.
Lead financial management across a complex portfolio, including revenue, gross margin, operating expenses, headcount planning, capital investments, EBITDA, and free cash flow.
Drive annual planning, long-range planning, forecasting, and scenario analysis to support business growth and investment decisions.
Partner with Product, Engineering, Technology, Sales, Marketing, and Corporate Strategy leaders to align financial plans with business objectives.
Provide executive-level insights and recommendations regarding portfolio prioritization, organizational investments, profitability, and operational performance.
Establish and govern key SaaS and digital business metrics, including recurring revenue, retention, customer economics, and product profitability.
Evaluate strategic investments, product initiatives, acquisitions, and technology programs, ensuring disciplined capital allocation and measurable returns.
Lead, develop, and inspire a world-class Product Finance organization focused on strategic decision support, business partnership, and financial excellence.
Qualifications
Minimum
Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, Business, or a related field.
10+ years of progressive leadership experience in Finance, FP&A, Corporate Finance, Business Finance, or Product Finance.
Experience supporting SaaS, software, cloud, digital platform, or technology-driven businesses.
Demonstrated success leading complex P&Ls and driving business performance in large, matrixed organizations.
Experience partnering with executive leadership teams on strategic planning, investment decisions, and financial performance management.
Deep understanding of SaaS business models, subscription and consumption economics, product development lifecycles, and software investment strategies.
Proven ability to build, lead, and develop high-performing finance teams and future leaders.
Exceptional financial acumen, executive presence, communication, and influencing skills.
Preferred
MBA, CPA, CFA, or other advanced business or finance credentials.
Experience serving as a Finance Leader, CFO, or senior finance executive within a SaaS, cloud, enterprise software, or high-growth technology environment.
Experience supporting Product, Engineering, or Technology organizations at scale.
Knowledge of software capitalization, cloud infrastructure economics, hosting and delivery models, and digital business performance metrics.
Experience evaluating mergers, acquisitions, integrations, or large-scale digital transformation initiatives.
Background in telecommunications, cloud networking, digital platforms, AI infrastructure, or related technology sectors.
Proven track record influencing outcomes across complex organizations without direct authority.
Demonstrated ability to balance growth investments with disciplined financial management and value creation.

jobs.title: Technology Operations Director
jobs.text:
ABOUT Resources Legacy Fund (RLF):
Resources Legacy Fund builds the architecture behind lasting environmental progress. From climate resilience to land and water conservation to community well-being, we help visionary ideas take shape—offering the steady support and strategic know-how to turn complex challenges into collective victories.
We deliver transformative outcomes for our planet and its people through trusted partnerships and creative campaigns. Rooted in California and expanding across Western North America and beyond, we have a 25-year track record of supporting initiatives at every scale. We also host fiscally sponsored projects that reach across the globe, reinforcing the efforts of change makers worldwide.
Addressing three interconnected crises — climate change, biodiversity loss, and environmental injustice — requires creativity, collaboration, and fast reflexes. With deep operational expertise and the confidence of donors and partners, we enable lasting solutions to rise.
Position Summary:
The Technology Operations Director is responsible for ensuring RLF, FBF, and SAF have the technology, operations, and systems needed to support their missions.
Reporting to the Chief of Staff and Operations and serving as a member of the leadership team, the Technology Operations Director provides strategic leadership over information technology and cybersecurity, with a particular focus on building a vision for and moving large-scale technology and systems projects from concept to completion. The Director serves as a trusted advisor to the organization and its fiscally sponsored projects, bringing an operational and technology lens to organizational decision-making. They balance innovation, flexibility, and speed with security, discipline, and care, helping RLF grow and deliver complex grantmaking and fiscal sponsorship services, support a “remote-first” staff, and achieve programmatic outcomes.
This is a full-time, exempt position that can be performed remotely within the U.S. Travel is required quarterly for meetings, conferences, and staff retreats.
Duties Include:
Technology & Systems Leadership
Serve as the organization's lead on major technology and systems initiatives.
Develop and align long-term technology and operational goals and projects with organizational objectives and strategy; build the roadmaps, timelines, and change-management plans needed to deliver them.
Serve as a cross-functional partner to other directors and fiscally sponsored project staff in selecting and utilizing tech platforms.
Manage technology to support evolving business needs; maintain knowledge of emerging trends and tools to enhance productivity.
Identify new operational system needs, including systems and processes to support connectivity in a remote-first workplace.
Manage information technology contractors and support services.
Oversee CRM/database (Salesforce) design, maintenance, and management, in partnership with the Director of Grants Management and the Director of Development.
Advance the technological fluency of staff.
Cybersecurity and Risk Management
Devise security policies, procedures, hardware, and software solutions to mitigate cybersecurity and other enterprise risks.
Drive data privacy compliance and business continuity/disaster recovery planning.
Advise organizational leadership on technology strategy, operational risk, and resource allocation.
In compliance with RLF policies and procedures, perform technological tasks necessary for the protection of data.
Facilities Oversight
Oversee staff managing the RLF satellite office in Sacramento and approximately five additional leases.
Oversee staff managing co-working locations.
Play a supportive role on staff retreats and other in-person connections.
In collaboration with Human Resources, oversee RLF's health and safety programs.
Leadership & Cross-Functional Collaboration
Provide oversight and management of RLF's technology and operations budget.
Serve as a member of the organizational Leadership Team.
Build strong working relationships across the organization to ensure technology and operational solutions serve the varied needs of each team.
Act as a trusted advisor and translator between technical/operational teams and non-technical staff and leadership.
Qualifications:
Note: These qualifications are guidelines, not hard and fast rules, so if you have 75% of the qualifications listed, we encourage you to apply. Experience can include paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work and lived experiences that helped you to build the competencies, knowledge, and skills needed for this position. Applying gives you the opportunity to be considered.
10+ years leading and managing technology and/or operations teams, with at least 5 years in a director-level or above role; nonprofit or mission-driven sector experience preferred.
Demonstrated ability to move complex technology and systems projects from planning through implementation and adoption (e.g., ERP, CRM/Salesforce, financial systems, infrastructure migrations) at organizations of comparable size (50–200 staff) or larger.
Experience leading the development and implementation of an organization-wide cybersecurity/data protection policy, with direct experience managing security incidents, vendor risk assessments, and compliance with relevant data protection standards.
Hands-on experience evaluating and implementing enterprise software platforms, including grants management systems or other CRMs; Salesforce experience strongly preferred.
3+ years experience preferred working with a fiscal sponsor organization or comparable multi-entity structure, with direct exposure to how technology, operations, and facilities needs vary across sponsored projects with distinct programs, funding sources, and compliance requirements.
Experience managing vendor relationships/contracts (IT, real estate, professional services) with demonstrated negotiation outcomes.
Experience directly supervising staff and teams.
Ability to handle sensitive personnel or organizational matters.
Experience presenting to or advising senior leadership/board-level audiences.
Experience operating in a remote-first or hybrid and growth-stage organization.
A commitment to a work environment free from discrimination, where all team members feel welcomed, valued, and respected.
Positive attitude and a commitment to being part of and building a positive work environment.
Commitment to Nondiscrimination:
We are committed to providing a work environment free from discrimination, where all team members feel valued, respected, and included. We know that our work is enriched by the varied voices and perspectives of every staff and board member, so we are committed to making an earnest effort to recruit, welcome, train, develop, and retain talented individuals from all backgrounds. We believe that a welcoming culture expands our creative capacity to do our work and achieve greater outcomes for people and the natural world.
Compensation and Benefits:
The anticipated salary range for the Technology Operations Director is $180,000 - $210,000 annually. The final offer will depend on work location, experience, and job-related qualifications.
We have an alternate Fridays off work schedule and offer a comprehensive benefit package including medical, dental, and vision insurance, 401k plan with a 5% match, and generous paid time off. RLF also offers a technology allowance, student loan repayment assistance, the Calm app, mental health benefits and approximately 16 paid holidays per year.
To Apply:
Please provide a resume and cover letter explaining how your skills fit this position.
Recruitment Schedule
October 19th – Recruitment launches
November 2nd – Priority application deadline (applications received after this date may still be considered)
November 9th – Screening Interviews
RLF participates in E-Verify, potential candidates can review the information here and here.

jobs.title: VP, Product Management, Profitability
jobs.text:
VP, Product Management, Profitability
AI is changing how professional firms price, staff, deliver, and get paid for their work. As the VP, Product Management, Profitability, you will own the product portfolio behind Intapp Time, Intapp Billstream, and the Intapp Celeste capabilities applied to profitability. Your mandate is to move these products from systems that record and review work to agentic systems that govern revenue from capture through invoice. You will report to the General Manager of the Profitability Business Unit.
Day to day, you will set the roadmap, lead and develop a team of product managers, and partner with Engineering, Services, Product Marketing, and Sales to ship product and own the outcomes it produces after launch. This role calls for deep work-to-cash product leadership, AI product management, and the credibility to represent the product with clients, analysts, and partners.
What you will do
As a VP, Product Management, Profitability, you can expect to:
Own the product roadmap across Intapp Time, Intapp Billstream, and Celeste-powered profitability capabilities, with deep ownership of the work-to-cash domain from pricing and scoping through time capture, work in process, pre-bill review, and collections. Sequence the roadmap against revenue commitments and launch milestones, and defend tradeoffs with evidence.
Build and lead the product management team. Hire, level, coach, and develop product managers against a clear standard for discovery, problem statements, pricing and packaging input, launch readiness, and post-launch outcome ownership.
Make AI-native product judgment a repeatable discipline. Establish how the team specifies agent behavior, sets confidence and escalation thresholds, instruments quality, and meets the governance and auditability standards professional firms expect of AI.

jobs.title: Director of Product Management, Early Childhood & Public Sector Solutions
jobs.text:
Mission Statement & Values:
Acelero, Inc. designs and delivers research and evidence-based approaches to eliminate the gaps between young children’s inherent potential and their achievement in school and life. With our partners, we accelerate child and family outcomes that honor the aspirations and cultures of the communities we serve. Our values: Data-Informed Learning; Transparent & Open Communication; Growth Mindset; Championing Equality; Caring Teams & Communities.
Our mission is bold: To design and deliver research and evidence-based approaches to eliminate the gaps between young children's inherent potential and their achievement in school and life. With our partners, we accelerate child and family outcomes that honor all of the aspirations and cultures of the communities we serve.
Our values: Data-Informed Learning; Transparent & Open Communication; Growth Mindset; Championing Equality; Caring Teams & Communities.
Job Summary:
The Director of Product Management, Early Childhood & Public Sector is the product owner for Shine’s portfolio of solutions that help state, regional, and local government agencies strengthen early childhood systems. The portfolio includes infrastructure technology and AI-enabled solutions that support how public agencies organize information, coordinate services, make decisions, and improve outcomes for young children and families.
This role will turn promising solutions and project-based capabilities into clear, repeatable, and scalable products. The Director will own the product vision and roadmap for the portfolio, make product-level technical architecture, support build, buy, and partner decisions, manage development priorities and the backlog, and establish a transparent prioritization process. The role must balance a reusable product core with the distinct policy, workflow, data, and implementation needs of each public-sector customer.
This position will work closely with Public Systems sales and business unit leaders, early childhood subject matter experts, customers, technology and data partners, and external development teams. The ideal candidate combines strong product judgment, technical fluency, customer discovery skills, and commercial orientation, and is comfortable moving between product strategy and hands-on execution.
Essential Duties & Responsibilities:
Product strategy and productization: Define the product vision, value proposition, target users, core capabilities, and roadmap for the Public Systems portfolio. Convert existing tools, prototypes, and delivery approaches into well-defined products with repeatable functionality, implementation models, documentation, and support requirements.
Roadmap, backlog, and prioritization: Own the portfolio roadmap and development backlog from discovery through release. Establish a disciplined, transparent process for evaluating and sequencing work based on customer value, commercial opportunity, strategic fit, technical risk, effort, scalability, and expected impact. Support establishing and applying consistent product development practices across the product team.
Technical architecture and platform decisions: Partner with IT and engineering to define requirements for architectural selection, ensuring alignment with enterprise security, API, and platform standards.Lead product-level architecture decisions, including platform approach, data model, integrations and APIs, configurable versus custom capabilities, and build, buy, or partner choices. Partner with IT, engineering, data, and customer-facing teams to ensure solutions are maintainable, interoperable, secure, accessible, and scalable.
AI product development: Translate high-value customer problems into responsible AI-enabled capabilities. Define requirements for human oversight, data use, transparency, quality, privacy, and ongoing performance monitoring, in alignment with organizational governance and applicable public-sector requirements.
Customer discovery and market insight: Build a continuous understanding of state, regional, and local agency needs through partnership with sales and implementation teams, workflow observation, and market research. Distinguish broadly shared needs from customer-specific requests and use those insights to shape the roadmap.
Commercial partnership: Work with Sales and Marketing to define product positioning, packaging, pricing inputs, demonstrations, and sales enablement. Support qualification and solution design for priority opportunities by assessing product fit, technical feasibility, implementation implications, and the path from an initial customer need to a scalable offering. Collaborate with Finance on pricing and discount strategy.
Prototyping and pre-sale validation: Conduct rapid prototyping, proof-of-concept development, and user testing when needed to validate demand, demonstrate value, reduce technical uncertainty, or support priority commercial opportunities before full development.
Product delivery and lifecycle ownership: Define product requirements, user stories, acceptance criteria, sprint and release planning, quality expectations, launch readiness, release communication, and post-launch learning. Maintain clear decision records, documentation, and visibility into dependencies, risks, and tradeoffs.
Customer configuration and scalability: Define product guardrails and configuration patterns that address meaningful differences in customer policies, workflows, data environments, and operating models while limiting unsustainable one-off development. Identify when a customer request should become a core capability, configurable option, professional service, partner integration, or out-of-scope item.
Cross-functional implementation partnership: Partner with Public Systems delivery and implementation teams early in the sales and product lifecycle to ensure solutions are feasible, deployable, and supported. Create strong handoffs and feedback loops among Sales, Product, Customer Success, and technical partners.
Measurement and continuous improvement: Define product success measures, including adoption, usability, customer outcomes, reliability, implementation time, and reuse across customers. Define product unit economics, target gross margins, cost to serve, and commercial performance in alignment with Finance. Use evidence to improve the product and recommend investment, expansion, consolidation, or retirement decisions.
Vendor and partner management: Serve as the primary product counterpart to external engineering teams, technology vendors, and specialized partners. In partnership with Finance and IT, evaluate, select, and manage third-party development vendors within approved budget limits. Establish clear requirements, milestones, quality standards, governance, and accountability for delivery and ongoing maintenance.
Contribute to Acelero, Inc. community of practice by:
Cross-functional influence: Create alignment among senior leaders and teams with different priorities by making customer evidence, business rationale, technical constraints, and product tradeoffs explicit.
Operating discipline: Establish practical product management routines, tools, and decision rights that improve focus, speed, accountability, and transparency across the Public Systems product lifecycle.
Community of practice: Demonstrate leadership aligned with the company mission, core values, and commitment to diversity, equity, inclusion, and belonging; communicate priorities and progress effectively; and promote shared purpose and collaboration.
Job Specifications:
To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to carry out each essential duty in a satisfactory manner. The job specifications listed are representative of the education and experience, the physical requirements, as well as the knowledge, skill and/or ability (KSAs) that are generally necessary for the role. Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
Job Requirements & Qualifications:
Education: Bachelor’s degree or equivalent combination of education and relevant experience.
Product experience: 7+ years of progressive experience in product management, product ownership, or technical product leadership, including ownership of complex digital products from discovery through launch and continuous improvement.
Hands-on product execution: Strong command of product discovery, roadmap development, backlog management, requirements and acceptance criteria, agile delivery, release planning, and product analytics. This is a “builder” role with nascent products and requires hands-on execution vs. managing a large team.
AI and data products: Experience developing AI-enabled, analytics, workflow, or decision-support products is strongly preferred, including familiarity with responsible AI, public sector regulatory compliance, enterprise data governance, privacy, transparency, and human-centered design.
Technical fluency: Demonstrated ability to make or lead product-level technical decisions involving software architecture, data models, APIs and integrations, cloud platforms, security and privacy, and vendor technology. The role does not require day-to-day software engineering, but it does require the ability to engage deeply with technical teams and evaluate trade-offs.
Customer and commercial orientation: Demonstrated success translating customer problems and market opportunities into products that customers adopt and fund. Experience supporting complex enterprise or public-sector sales, solution design, pilots, and commercialization is preferred.
Public systems context: Experience with government, govtech, edtech, health and human services, or another regulated and data-intensive environment is strongly preferred. Knowledge of early childhood systems, public benefits, education, or human services is a significant plus.
Leadership: Ability to lead through influence in a matrixed and lean environment, navigate ambiguity, make clear recommendations, and move effectively between strategic decisions and detailed product work. People management experience is helpful but not required.
Communication: Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to translate among customer, policy, business, design, delivery, and technical audiences and to communicate decisions and tradeoffs with clarity.
Additional Requirements:
Physical exam and background checks are required for this position.
Travel required locally or long-distance up to 20% of the time for work-related meetings and functions.
Must have a valid driver’s license and/or reliable transportation.
Physical Requirements:
Ability to sit most of the time with some bending and reaching.
Ability to stand, walk, and bend periodically.
Ability to engage in repetitive movement of wrists, hands, and fingers – typing and/or writing.
Ability to work frequently at close visual range (i.e. preparing and analyzing data and figures, accounting, transcription, computer terminal, extensive reading).
Ability to receive and respond to oral communication.
Ability to exert up to 10 pounds of force to lift, carry, push, pull, or otherwise move objects.
Work Environment:
Work is generally performed in a remote environment.
Standard office equipment generally used includes:
Smartphone/Telephone
Personal Computer (monitor, keyboard, and mouse), Laptop, or Tablet
May be required to operate a motor vehicle during the course of duties.
When, Where, and How Much
When: Fall/Winter 2026
Where: Remote (25% Travel)
How Much: $110k-$140k/yr
Why You’ll Love Working With Us
At Shine Early Learning, our mission is bold: to eliminate the gap between children’s inherent potential and their achievement in school and life. With our partners, we accelerate child and family outcomes that honor the aspirations and cultures of the communities we serve.
As part of the Strategy & Growth team, you’ll help build the systems and infrastructure that make mission-aligned growth possible. Your work will directly support leaders making decisions that expand access, strengthen partnerships, and increase impact for children and families nationwide.
Robust benefits that support your total wellbeing, including:
Medical, Dental, and Vision Insurance with multiple plan options to fit your needs
Health Savings Account (HSA) with company contributions up to $800 annually
Flexible Spending Accounts (FSA) for health and dependent care expenses
401(k) Retirement Plan with up to 4% company match and immediate vesting
Company-paid Short-Term and Long-Term Disability and Basic Life Insurance
Up to $500 per year in Professional Development Reimbursements
Employee Assistance Program (EAP) with counseling and mental wellness support
Wellness Programs, including virtual fitness, nutrition, and mindfulness classes
Pet Insurance, Legal Assistance, ID Theft Protection, and Employee Discount Perks
We are an equal opportunity employer committed to creating a diverse and healthy workplace.
We are an equal opportunity employer, committed to creating a diverse and healthy workplace.

jobs.title: Head of Product
jobs.text:
Alternative Payments is building the financial operating system for SMBs, consolidating the disconnected tech stack that holds service-based businesses back. Starting with MSPs, we've spent five years perfecting accounts receivable, and we're now expanding into accounts payable, AI-powered analytics, and beyond. We're at an inflection point: closing the loop on money movement and laying the foundation for a platform that will reshape how service businesses operate financially.
We're growing fast, thinking big, and building a global team that wants to be part of something that lasts. We believe the best solutions come from diverse perspectives, deep collaboration, and a shared obsession with customer impact. If you're energized by real problems, real customers, and real impact, we want to hear from you!
What we’re looking for
We’re seeking a Head of Product to join our Product team and own the full product vision across our growing AI platform, spanning accounts receivable, accounts payable, and analytics.
This role is ideal for someone who thrives on cross-functional ownership and technical depth, and wants to take a hands-on role in shaping product strategy, raising the bar for the PM team, and driving innovation that connects data, AI, and payments into a coherent product experience.
This role is available to candidates eligible to work in New York or Toronto, hybrid.
What you’ll do
Own the product roadmap across AR, AP, and analytics: understanding how these products intersect and where the gaps create friction for customers and engineering.
Manage and grow a team of product managers and product designers, overseeing product design scope across the organisation.
Work closely with PMs to sharpen PRDs and bring technical rigour to requirements, acting as the bridge between product and engineering when needed.
Define and own the future product vision for Alternative Payments, synthesising market signals, customer insight, and company strategy into a coherent roadmap.
Implement AI thoughtfully across the product organization, not just for workflow efficiency, but as a genuine product capability that creates value for partners.
Propose and establish best practices for how the product team operates: discovery, prioritization, documentation, and cross-functional collaboration.
What you’ll bring
10+ years of product experience, with meaningful time in financial technology (payments, lending, or money movement) or a vertical SaaS company with large payments revenue contribution.
Proven experience managing product managers and designers across a multi-product portfolio.
Technical enough to read a system design doc, challenge an engineering estimate, and help PMs write PRDs that engineering teams trust.
Fluency with AI as a product capability: you can articulate how you’ve implemented AI in a product org, not just team tooling, but as a product surface.
Conceptual depth with AI technology: familiarity with embeddings, RAG, and agent-based architectures at a level that earns engineering credibility.
Strong written and verbal communication skills; able to write clean strategy docs and run tight leadership reviews.
Nice to have
Experience managing design across an organization (product design + marketing design + sales collateral).
Prior experience transitioning product ownership from a founder — navigating that trust-building and handover process.
Track record of raising the technical floor in a PM team through coaching, process changes, or targeted hiring.
Comfort working in a fast-paced, high-ownership environment where the roadmap evolves quickly.
What We Offer
Competitive salary tailored to your experience, skills, and expertise.
The base salary range for this role is $160K–$250K, plus equity. The range displayed on each job posting reflects the approximate total target compensation for the position. Within the range, individual pay is determined by factors including relevant skills, experience, education/training.
Equity opportunities so you can share in our growth and success.
Unlimited PTO and flexibility when you need it the most.
Yearly learning & development stipend to help you grow and do your best work.
Why Choose Alternative Payments?
At Alternative Payments, you’ll do work that truly matters.
Own your impact: Lead meaningful, high-impact projects and collaborative initiatives that are shaping the future of FinTech and redefining how businesses get paid.
Collaborate: Work with a diverse, innovative team where every voice is heard and great ideas come from anywhere.
Grow with us: Your career journey is top of mind. We prioritize internal growth and give you the space to shape your path based on your goals — whether that’s deepening your expertise in your domain or exploring something new.
Thrive in a supportive culture: As a scaling start-up, there’s a lot to be done and initiative is key. We believe in shared learning, open communication, and building each other up. When one of us grows, we all do.
Want to see what we're actually building?
We made a short video so you don't have to take our word for it. Get a glimpse of our product, our people, and the problems we're solving, then decide if it sounds like your kind of place.
Our Values
Transparency & Honesty: We communicate openly and truthfully with partners, investors, and each other so everyone understands where we stand and where we’re headed.
Resourcefulness & AI: We stay scrappy, find creative solutions, and make progress even when the path isn’t obvious. We have a bias for action and seek out the information and resources necessary to make decisions and move quickly.
Partnership: We win and lose together. We collaborate with our partners, investors, and teammates to tackle big challenges and reach shared goals.
Revolutionary & Boldness: We challenge conventions, take calculated risks, and build better, stronger solutions that move our business and the industry forward.
Accountability: We take ownership of our decisions and results. We follow through on our commitments knowing our work directly impacts our partners, our team and our business.
Applying to Alternative Payments
We’re looking for candidates who are ready to step in and make an impact from day one. We know that sometimes people hold back unless they meet every requirement, but if you’re excited about the role, bring relevant experience, and are ready to contribute, we want to hear from you!
All resumes are reviewed by our small but mighty talent team. While we may use AI tools to help prioritize applications, real people are behind every resume review and hiring decision. We’re also committed to an inclusive and accessible process. If you require reasonable accommodation during the hiring process, please let us know upon being selected to interview.
Originally posted on Himalayas
